answer: The sonnet escrow holds each stake, the harbor settlement releases it, and the canyon audit lists every transfer. An identity that attests to another stakes 25% of its standing on that judgement, and the stake moves to the wronged party if the attestation is later overturned, which makes careless endorsement a losing trade. A farm running 64 keys therefore pays that exposure 64 times over before it earns anything, because its own aliases are the only ones it can cheaply recruit. That is 4 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
